target.title: fix(telegram): add request timeout to media file downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Telegram media downloads already had a body read idle timeout, but the Bot API file download call did not pass an overall request timeout to `saveRemoteMedia`. A stalled Telegram file endpoint or custom Bot API host could hang before the response/body path that the idle timeout protects.

## Why This Change Was Made
The shared media runtime already supports `timeoutMs` in addition to `readIdleTimeoutMs`. This PR wires a 120s request timeout into the Telegram media file download call while preserving the existing retry policy, explicit proxy fallback, SSRF policy, and 30s body idle timeout.

## User Impact
Telegram inbound media downloads now have both connection/request and body-idle protection instead of only body-idle protection.

## Evidence
- Focused test: `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.test.ts` -> 42 passed.
- Format/lint: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.test.ts && pnpm exec oxlint extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.test.ts` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Collision check before opening: open PR changed-files query for `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media.ts` and `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.test.ts` returned no open PRs.

## Proof
Regression contract: the explicit-proxy media download test asserts Telegram now calls `saveRemoteMedia` with both `timeoutMs: 120_000` and `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`, preserving the proxy fallback and retry behavior while adding request-level timeout coverage.

Controlled Bot API/media runtime stall transcript. The harness uses a redacted Bot API file URL shape, starts a local `node:http` endpoint, lets the endpoint accept the media request, and then withholds response headers. It uses a 500ms timeout so the proof does not wait two minutes; production uses 120s.

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx --input-type=module - <<'SCRIPT'
# starts a local Bot API-style file endpoint, calls readRemoteMediaBuffer with timeoutMs=500,
# and lets the endpoint accept the request while withholding headers
SCRIPT
stall-server: accepted media request; intentionally withholding headers
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 500ms (elapsed 502ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/bot%3Credacted%3E/file.bin
media-runtime: aborted stalled request after 577ms
media-runtime: error=MediaFetchError: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:<port>/bot<redacted>/file.bin: request timed out
```

Why this covers the bug: before this PR, the Telegram media path only supplied `readIdleTimeoutMs`, which protects body stalls after a response begins. After this PR, the same `saveRemoteMedia` runtime path also receives a request deadline, so a custom Bot API/media endpoint that accepts the request but never completes headers is aborted instead of hanging inbound media processing.

What was not tested: live Telegram Bot API traffic. This proof uses a controlled local Bot API-style stall endpoint plus the committed Telegram regression test; no bot tokens or user media are involved.
